//: askfirst rules. Keys starting with // are comments; askfirst ignores them.
//actions: allow | ask | deny | pass | agent. Firmness: allow < pass < agent < ask < deny.
//unseen: What happens to a signature with no rule and no verdict: ask (queue it, instant), agent (judge it, 6-8s), deny, or pass.

agent.//: The judge for action=agent, unseen=agent and `askfirst review --agent`.
agent.//timeout: Keep the PreToolUse hook timeout in settings.json comfortably above this.

//rules: Apply in every mode. A mode may tighten these, never loosen them.

rules.reason: Pushing publishes work. Confirm the remote and branch.
rules.context: The user requires a prompt before any push, whatever the program or alias. Wait for their answer; do not retry through a script, a wrapper or a different spelling.
Force push is denied. Use --force-with-lease and ask the user first, or rebase locally and push normally.
Force push is denied. Use --force-with-lease and ask the user first, or rebase locally and push normally.

reader.description: Read and investigate. Anything that changes state is refused.

rules.context: askfirst is in reader mode, which investigates without changing anything. Report what you found and let the user switch to contributor mode if they want the change made.

rules.reason: reader mode does not stage changes.
rules.context: askfirst is in reader mode. Do not stage or commit; describe the change you would make instead.

rules.reason: reader mode does not publish anything.
rules.context: askfirst is in reader mode, which never publishes. Do not push. Tell the user what you would have pushed.

contributor.description: Edit, build, test and commit. Publishing and discarding still ask.

rules.context: A hard reset throws away uncommitted changes. Confirm with the user what would be lost before running it.

godmode.description: Everything runs. Shared rules and the self-guard still apply.
godmode.//: A catch-all allow. The shared rules still apply (a push still asks, a force push is still denied) and the self-guard is compiled in, so askfirst's own config still asks.
